preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or have compromised the owner's private key)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the setBlacklist() function to blacklist any target address. This will prevent the blacklisted address from making any transfers, effectively freezing their tokens. The exploit demonstrates owner's excessive control over user transactions.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has a setBlacklist() function that is only callable by the owner (onlyOwner modifier). This function can blacklist any address, preventing them from transferring tokens. This demonstrates excessive owner control where the owner can freeze any user's tokens arbitrarily.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Get the current owner address of the contract. 2. Impersonate the owner using vm.prank(). 3. Call setBlacklist() on the target contract to blacklist a victim address. 4. Verify that isBlacklist[victim] is now true.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. In setUp(), we don't need any special setup since we're just calling a function. 2. In testExploit(), first get the owner address by calling the owner() function on the contract. 3. Use vm.prank(owner) to impersonate the owner. 4. Call TARGET.setBlacklist(victimAddress, true). 5. Verify the blacklist status is true.
